about: Single source of truth for what the F4P Hub collects and how it is scored. The weekly pipeline (f4p_weekly_update.py), the Data Hunt manual prompts and the Data Hunt Compare view all read this file. Change a definition here, run build_prompt_pack.py, and all three agree.

hub_indicator_names: Central Bank Rate & Current Policy Stance

indicators.where_to_find: Click 'Manufacturing' under Reports → PMI number is in the FIRST sentence of the report. Above 50 = expansion.
indicators.scoring_guide: +2 above 52 & rising · +1 above 50 · 0 near 50 · -1 below 50 · -2 below 48 & falling.

indicators.where_to_find: Same ISM site → Click 'Services' tab → NMI headline number in the first paragraph.
indicators.scoring_guide: Services = 70% of US GDP. +2 above 56 · +1 above 52 · 0 near 50 · -1 below 50 · -2 below 47.

indicators.where_to_find: University of Michigan site → Large bold number at the top is the Index of Consumer Sentiment.
indicators.scoring_guide: +2 above 80 or strongly rising · +1 above 70 · 0 stable 60-70 · -1 below 60 · -2 below 55 & falling.

indicators.where_to_find: FRED → PERMIT series → read the latest value (thousands of units, seasonally adjusted annual rate) and the value for the same month a year earlier; both are on the chart.
indicators.scoring_guide: Score the change over the last year (latest month against the same month a year earlier), not the change from last month: +2 up more than 10% · +1 up 2% to 10% · 0 moved by less than 2% either way · -1 down 2% to 10% · -2 down more than 10%.

hub_series.calc: latest value (thousands, seasonally adjusted annual rate)

indicators.where_to_find: FRED → M2SL (monthly, seasonally adjusted) → use the latest monthly reading and its year-over-year % change (that month versus the same month a year earlier). Do not switch to the weekly M2 series; if M2SL has not published the newest month yet, report its latest month and say so.
indicators.scoring_guide: +2 M2 expanding >5% YoY · +1 expanding 2-5% · 0 flat · -1 contracting · -2 contracting sharply (deflationary).

indicators.hub_name: Central Bank Rate & Current Policy Stance
indicators.where_to_find: Fed H.15 release → Find 'Federal funds (effective)' rate. Also check latest FOMC statement for direction (hiking/hold/cutting).
indicators.scoring_guide: +2 hiking cycle or strong hawkish hold · +1 hold with hawkish lean · 0 neutral hold · -1 dovish lean · -2 cutting cycle.

hub_series.calc: latest value (rate number only; the stance still needs reading from the FOMC statement)

indicators.where_to_find: BLS CPI page → Click latest News Release → '12-month percent change, All items' is in the first table.
indicators.scoring_guide: +2 above 3.5% & rising · +1 above 2.5% · 0 near 2% target · -1 below 1.5% · -2 below 1% or falling sharply.

hub_series.calc: year-over-year % change of the seasonally adjusted index (compared with the reading for the same month one year earlier)

indicators.where_to_find: Same BLS CPI release → Find 'All items less food and energy' row → annual % change column.
indicators.scoring_guide: Fed's most watched number. +2 above 3% sticky · +1 above 2.5% · 0 near 2.5% · -1 easing toward 2% · -2 falling sharply.

hub_series.calc: year-over-year % change of the seasonally adjusted index (compared with the reading for the same month one year earlier)

indicators.where_to_find: BLS PPI page → Latest News Release → 'Final demand' 12-month % change in the first paragraph.
indicators.scoring_guide: Leads CPI by 1-3 months. +2 above 4% & rising · +1 above 2% · 0 near 2% · -1 falling · -2 below 0% deflation.

hub_series.calc: year-over-year % change of the seasonally adjusted Final Demand index (compared with the reading for the same month one year earlier)

indicators.where_to_find: Same BLS PPI release → Look for 'Final demand less foods, energy, and trade' — this is Core PPI. Note % change.
indicators.scoring_guide: Most reliable pipeline signal. +2 above 3% · +1 above 2% · 0 near 2% · -1 falling · -2 below 1%.

hub_series.calc: year-over-year % change of the seasonally adjusted Final Demand less foods, energy and trade services index (compared with the reading for the same month one year earlier)

indicators.where_to_find: BLS Employment Situation → 'Total nonfarm' change in thousands is the bold number in the first paragraph. Compare to forecast.
indicators.scoring_guide: +2 strong beat vs forecast · +1 mild beat · 0 in line · -1 mild miss · -2 large miss (recession signal).

indicators.where_to_find: FRED → GFDEGDQ188S → Chart shows federal debt as % of GDP. Note current level and trend direction.
indicators.scoring_guide: Score the change over the last year (latest figure against the one a year earlier): +1 falling or stable (no rise) · 0 rising by less than 1 point of GDP · -1 rising by 1 to 4 points · -2 rising by more than 4 points (markets demanding a higher yield premium).

indicators.where_to_find: FRED → FYFSGDA188S (federal surplus or deficit as a percent of GDP, annual; negative = deficit) → read the latest year and the year before.
indicators.scoring_guide: Score the change in the budget balance as a % of GDP (latest full year against the year before): +1 surplus, or deficit narrowed by 0.5 point or more · 0 deficit moved by less than 0.5 point · -1 deficit widened by 0.5 to 1.5 points · -2 deficit widened by more than 1.5 points (a surplus that falls into deficit counts as widening).

indicators.where_to_find: FRED → DGS10 (daily) → read the latest daily value and the value from about a week earlier; both are on the chart.
indicators.scoring_guide: Rising = higher USD return attracting capital. Score the change in the yield over the last 7 days (latest daily value against the value on the same weekday one week earlier, or the nearest earlier trading day): +2 up more than 0.25 point · +1 up 0.05 to 0.25 · 0 moved by less than 0.05 either way · -1 down 0.05 to 0.25 · -2 down more than 0.25 point.

indicators.where_to_find: FRED → WALCL (weekly, millions of dollars) → read the latest value and the value from the same week a year earlier; both are on the chart.
indicators.scoring_guide: Shrinking = QT = hawkish; aggressive expansion = currency dilution. Score the change in total assets (the ratio to GDP is not needed) over the last year, latest weekly or monthly figure against the same date a year earlier: +2 down more than 10% · +1 down 2% to 10% · 0 moved by less than 2% either way · -1 up 2% to 10% · -2 up more than 10%.

indicators.where_to_find: S&P Global PMI → Search 'Eurozone Manufacturing' → Latest press release → PMI number in the headline figure.
indicators.scoring_guide: +2 above 52 & rising · +1 above 50 · 0 near 50 · -1 below 50 · -2 below 47 (deep contraction).

indicators.where_to_find: Same site → Filter 'Eurozone Services' or Composite → PMI headline figure in the release.
indicators.scoring_guide: EZ services has held up better than manufacturing. +2 above 54 · +1 above 51 · 0 near 50 · -1 below 50 · -2 below 47.

indicators.where_to_find: EC Business & Consumer Surveys → Monthly Consumer Confidence Indicator. Negative number is normal — look at trend direction vs prior month.
indicators.scoring_guide: +2 strongly rising month-over-month · +1 improving · 0 stable · -1 falling · -2 sharply negative & falling.

indicators.where_to_find: Destatis (German Statistics) → Building permits table → Find the latest monthly figure and the same month a year earlier (calculate the % change yourself if the page does not show it).
indicators.scoring_guide: German permits proxy for EZ construction health. Score the change over the last year (latest month against the same month a year earlier), not the change from last month: +2 up more than 10% · +1 up 2% to 10% · 0 moved by less than 2% either way · -1 down 2% to 10% · -2 down more than 10%.

indicators.where_to_find: ECB Statistics → M3 annual growth rate. Check if money supply is expanding or contracting.
indicators.scoring_guide: +2 M3 growing strongly (>5%) · +1 moderate growth · 0 flat · -1 contracting · -2 sharply contracting.

indicators.hub_name: Central Bank Rate & Current Policy Stance
indicators.where_to_find: ECB Key Interest Rates page → Find Deposit Facility Rate. Check latest ECB meeting statement for direction.
indicators.scoring_guide: +2 hiking or strong hawkish hold · +1 hold hawkish lean · 0 neutral hold · -1 dovish lean · -2 cutting cycle.

indicators.where_to_find: Eurostat HICP → Click latest Flash Estimate or News Release → Annual inflation rate % for Eurozone.
indicators.scoring_guide: +2 above 3% rising · +1 above 2.5% · 0 near 2% ECB target · -1 below 1.5% · -2 below 1% (deflation risk).

indicators.where_to_find: Same Eurostat HICP release → Look for 'All-items HICP excluding energy and food' — this is Core HICP.
indicators.scoring_guide: ECB's most watched inflation measure. Sticky core = hawkish ECB = EUR positive.

indicators.where_to_find: Eurostat Short-Term Statistics → Industry → Producer Prices. Find 'euro area' annual % change.
indicators.scoring_guide: Leads HICP by 1-3 months. Rising PPI = future inflation = ECB stays hawkish = EUR positive.

indicators.where_to_find: Same Eurostat page → Filter for ex-energy PPI (core). Note annual % change trend direction.
indicators.scoring_guide: Core PPI strips out energy volatility — shows underlying cost pressure. Rising = inflationary.

indicators.where_to_find: Eurostat Labour Market → Latest 'Euro area unemployment rate' monthly figure.
indicators.scoring_guide: Lower unemployment = stronger economy. +2 falling sharply · +1 falling · 0 stable · -1 rising · -2 rising sharply.

indicators.where_to_find: Eurostat Government Finance → Govt debt as % of GDP. Check latest annual figure and trend.
indicators.scoring_guide: High debt constrains ECB flexibility. Score the change over the last year (latest figure against the one a year earlier): +1 falling or stable (no rise) · 0 rising by less than 1 point of GDP · -1 rising by 1 to 4 points · -2 rising by more than 4 points.

indicators.where_to_find: Same Eurostat page → General government deficit/surplus as % of GDP. Use the budget balance as a % of GDP for the latest full year and for the year before (work out the % of GDP yourself if the page shows only a money amount).
indicators.scoring_guide: Score the change in the budget balance as a % of GDP (latest full year against the year before): +1 surplus, or deficit narrowed by 0.5 point or more · 0 deficit moved by less than 0.5 point · -1 deficit widened by 0.5 to 1.5 points · -2 deficit widened by more than 1.5 points (a surplus that falls into deficit counts as widening).

indicators.where_to_find: Bundesbank → Daily yields of current Federal securities → the 10-year Bund (series BBSSY.D.REN.EUR.A630.000000WT1010.A, daily yield of the current 10-year federal bond; PDF or CSV download) → read the latest daily value and the value from a week earlier.
indicators.scoring_guide: Germany = EZ benchmark. A sharp fall can signal risk-off or recession fear. Score the change in the yield over the last 7 days (latest daily value against the value on the same weekday one week earlier, or the nearest earlier trading day): +2 up more than 0.25 point · +1 up 0.05 to 0.25 · 0 moved by less than 0.05 either way · -1 down 0.05 to 0.25 · -2 down more than 0.25 point.

indicators.where_to_find: ECB → Weekly financial statements (consolidated financial statement of the Eurosystem, published weekly) → Total assets for the latest week and for the same week a year earlier.
indicators.scoring_guide: Shrinking = QT = hawkish. Score the change in total assets (the ratio to GDP is not needed) over the last year, latest weekly or monthly figure against the same date a year earlier: +2 down more than 10% · +1 down 2% to 10% · 0 moved by less than 2% either way · -1 up 2% to 10% · -2 up more than 10%.

indicators.where_to_find: S&P Global PMI → Filter 'United Kingdom Manufacturing' → PMI headline figure in latest release.
indicators.scoring_guide: UK manufacturing is smaller than services but signals export health. Score the headline PMI reading: +2 above 52 · +1 from 50.5 to 52 · 0 from 49.5 to 50.5 · -1 from 47 to 49.5 · -2 below 47.

indicators.where_to_find: Same S&P Global site → Filter 'UK Services' → PMI headline figure.
indicators.scoring_guide: MOST important PMI for GBP. UK is 80% services economy. Score the headline PMI reading: +2 above 55 · +1 from 52 to 55 · 0 from 50 to 52 · -1 from 47 to 50 · -2 below 47.

indicators.where_to_find: GfK UK Consumer Confidence → Monthly headline figure. Negative is normal — look at trend vs prior month.
indicators.scoring_guide: +2 strongly rising · +1 improving · 0 stable · -1 falling · -2 sharply negative & deteriorating.

indicators.where_to_find: BoE Statistics → Mortgage approvals for house purchase. Monthly figure in thousands. Also find the same month a year earlier, so the change over the year can be worked out (calculate the % change yourself if the page does not show it).
indicators.scoring_guide: Rising approvals = housing market recovery = confidence. Score the change over the last year (latest month against the same month a year earlier), not the change from last month: +2 up more than 10% · +1 up 2% to 10% · 0 moved by less than 2% either way · -1 down 2% to 10% · -2 down more than 10%.

indicators.where_to_find: BoE Money & Credit page → M4 annual growth rate in the latest release.
indicators.scoring_guide: M4 is BoE's preferred broad money measure. Score the year-on-year growth of M4: +2 above 6% · +1 from 2% to 6% · 0 from 0% to 2% · -1 from -2% to 0% · -2 below -2%.

indicators.hub_name: Central Bank Rate & Current Policy Stance
indicators.where_to_find: BoE page → Current Bank Rate shown in large bold text. Check latest MPC vote split for direction.
indicators.scoring_guide: Score the latest MPC decision and vote: +2 raised Bank Rate, or held while at least one MPC member voted to raise · +1 held with everyone voting to hold and the minutes or guidance leaning hawkish (rates may need to stay high or rise) · 0 held with a balanced message · -1 held with the message leaning dovish (cuts likely) or at least one member voting to cut · -2 cut Bank Rate. Judge the latest meeting only; earlier moves do not count.

indicators.where_to_find: ONS → Consumer price inflation → '12-month CPI rate' highlighted % box in the latest release.
indicators.scoring_guide: BoE targets 2%. Score the headline annual rate: +2 above 3.5% · +1 from 2.5% to 3.5% · 0 from 1.5% to 2.5% · -1 from 1% to 1.5% · -2 below 1%.

indicators.where_to_find: Same ONS CPI release → Find 'CPI excluding energy, food, alcohol & tobacco' — this is Core CPI.
indicators.scoring_guide: BoE watches services and core inflation closely; sticky core is hawkish and GBP positive. Score the annual rate with the same bands as headline CPI: +2 above 3.5% · +1 from 2.5% to 3.5% · 0 from 1.5% to 2.5% · -1 from 1% to 1.5% · -2 below 1%.

indicators.where_to_find: ONS PPI bulletin → 'Output PPI' annual % change in the headline figure.
indicators.scoring_guide: Rising output PPI = cost pressures passing through. Score the annual rate: +2 above 4% · +1 from 2% to 4% · 0 from 0% to 2% · -1 from -2% to 0% · -2 below -2%.

indicators.measure: Core output PPI (output prices excluding food, beverages, tobacco and petroleum), annual % change
indicators.where_to_find: ONS Producer price inflation bulletin (latest) → 'Core output' annual rate: output prices excluding food, beverages, tobacco and petroleum. Give the month it covers.
indicators.scoring_guide: Strips out energy and food, so it is the most reliable signal of underlying cost pressure. Score the annual rate with the same bands as headline PPI: +2 above 4% · +1 from 2% to 4% · 0 from 0% to 2% · -1 from -2% to 0% · -2 below -2%.

indicators.measure: UK unemployment rate (latest three months against the previous three months)
indicators.where_to_find: ONS Labour market overview (latest release) → 'Unemployment rate (aged 16 and over, seasonally adjusted)' for the latest three-month period, and the figure for the previous three-month period shown in the same release.
indicators.scoring_guide: Strong employment and low unemployment = BoE hawkish. Score the change in the unemployment rate (latest published rate against the previous published rate, both as shown by the source, to one decimal): +2 fell by 0.2 point or more · +1 fell by 0.1 point · 0 unchanged · -1 rose by 0.1 point · -2 rose by 0.2 point or more. Employment change is context only.

indicators.measure: General government gross debt, % of GDP (IMF World Economic Outlook, series GGXWDG_NGDP)
indicators.where_to_find: IMF DataMapper (open the JSON file at the source address; the same series is on imf.org/external/datamapper/GGXWDG_NGDP). Read the values for GBR for the last completed calendar year and the year before it. Ignore the current year and later years, which are forecasts. State which World Economic Outlook edition the data comes from.
indicators.scoring_guide: Score the change over the last year (last completed calendar year against the year before): +1 falling or stable (no rise) · 0 rising by less than 1 point of GDP · -1 rising by 1 to 4 points · -2 rising by more than 4 points.

indicators.measure: General government net lending (+) / borrowing (-), % of GDP (IMF World Economic Outlook, series GGXCNL_NGDP; a negative number is a deficit)
indicators.where_to_find: IMF DataMapper (open the JSON file at the source address; the same series is on imf.org/external/datamapper/GGXCNL_NGDP). Read the values for GBR for the last completed calendar year and the year before it. Ignore the current year and later years, which are forecasts. State which World Economic Outlook edition the data comes from.
indicators.scoring_guide: Score the change in the budget balance as a % of GDP (latest full year against the year before): +1 surplus, or deficit narrowed by 0.5 point or more · 0 deficit moved by less than 0.5 point · -1 deficit widened by 0.5 to 1.5 points · -2 deficit widened by more than 1.5 points (a surplus that falls into deficit counts as widening).

indicators.where_to_find: Bank of England Database → series IUDMNPY (10-year nominal par yield on British government securities, daily) → read the latest daily value and the value from a week earlier.
indicators.scoring_guide: Rising = higher GBP return = capital attracted. Score the change in the yield over the last 7 days (latest daily value against the value on the same weekday one week earlier, or the nearest earlier trading day): +2 up more than 0.25 point · +1 up 0.05 to 0.25 · 0 moved by less than 0.05 either way · -1 down 0.05 to 0.25 · -2 down more than 0.25 point.

indicators.where_to_find: BoE Balance Sheet statistics → Total assets → read the latest figure and the one from the same date a year earlier.
indicators.scoring_guide: Shrinking = QT = hawkish. Score the change in total assets (the ratio to GDP is not needed) over the last year, latest weekly or monthly figure against the same date a year earlier: +2 down more than 10% · +1 down 2% to 10% · 0 moved by less than 2% either way · -1 up 2% to 10% · -2 up more than 10%.

indicators.where_to_find: S&P Global PMI → Filter 'Japan Manufacturing' → PMI headline figure in latest release.
indicators.scoring_guide: Japan PMI tracks China demand. Score the headline PMI reading: +2 above 52 · +1 from 50.5 to 52 · 0 from 49.5 to 50.5 · -1 from 47 to 49.5 · -2 below 47.

indicators.where_to_find: Same site → Filter 'Japan Services' or 'Japan Composite' → PMI headline figure.
indicators.scoring_guide: Japan services sector has been resilient. Score the headline PMI reading: +2 above 54 · +1 from 51 to 54 · 0 from 50 to 51 · -1 from 47 to 50 · -2 below 47.

indicators.where_to_find: ESRI Japan → Consumer Confidence Survey → Monthly index number. Above 40 = positive sentiment.
indicators.scoring_guide: +2 above 44 & rising · +1 above 40 · 0 35-40 · -1 below 35 · -2 below 30 & falling sharply.

indicators.where_to_find: Japan Ministry of Land Infrastructure → Housing starts / permits data. Monthly figure in thousands. Also find the same month a year earlier, so the change over the year can be worked out (calculate the % change yourself if the page does not show it).
indicators.scoring_guide: Leads GDP by several months. Score the change over the last year (latest month against the same month a year earlier), not the change from last month: +2 up more than 10% · +1 up 2% to 10% · 0 moved by less than 2% either way · -1 down 2% to 10% · -2 down more than 10%.

indicators.measure: Japan M2 Money Supply (Bank of Japan Money Stock, M2 average amounts outstanding)
indicators.where_to_find: Bank of Japan → Statistics → Money Stock → latest monthly release → M2, year-on-year % change (average amounts outstanding). The old FRED Japan M2 series stopped in 2017, so do not use it.
indicators.scoring_guide: Score the year-on-year growth of M2: +2 above 4% · +1 from 2% to 4% · 0 from 0% to 2% · -1 from -2% to 0% · -2 below -2%.

indicators.hub_name: Central Bank Rate & Current Policy Stance
indicators.where_to_find: BoJ Monetary Policy → Latest statement → Policy-Rate Balance or Uncollateralised Overnight Call Rate.
indicators.scoring_guide: Score the latest BoJ decision: +2 raised the policy rate · +1 held, with the statement or at least one board member pointing toward a rise · 0 held with a balanced message and no clear next step · -1 held with the message staying clearly accommodative and no hint of a rise · -2 cut the rate or announced new easing. Judge the latest meeting only; earlier moves do not count.

indicators.where_to_find: Statistics Bureau Japan → CPI latest release → 'All items' year-on-year % change.
indicators.scoring_guide: Japan was deflationary for decades; the BoJ now looks for 2%. Score the headline annual rate: +2 above 2.5% · +1 from 2% to 2.5% · 0 from 1% to 2% · -1 from 0% to 1% · -2 below 0%.

indicators.where_to_find: Same Statistics Bureau page → 'All items less fresh food' = Japan Core CPI. Annual % change.
indicators.scoring_guide: BoJ watches core CPI (excluding fresh food); sustained above 2% is a rate-hike signal and JPY bullish. Score the annual rate with the same bands as headline CPI: +2 above 2.5% · +1 from 2% to 2.5% · 0 from 1% to 2% · -1 from 0% to 1% · -2 below 0%.

indicators.where_to_find: BoJ CGPI (Corporate Goods Price Index) → Annual rate in the latest release.
indicators.scoring_guide: Rising CGPI = import inflation passing through = can support BoJ normalization. Score the annual rate: +2 above 4% · +1 from 2% to 4% · 0 from 0% to 2% · -1 from -2% to 0% · -2 below -2%.

indicators.measure: Domestic CGPI excluding energy (electric power, city gas and water, petroleum and coal products), year-on-year %
indicators.where_to_find: BoJ Corporate Goods Price Index (latest release) → Domestic CGPI excluding electric power, gas and water and petroleum and coal products → year-on-year % change. Give the month it covers.
indicators.scoring_guide: Core CGPI excluding energy is the BoJ's cleaner pipeline signal. Score the annual rate with the same bands as headline PPI: +2 above 4% · +1 from 2% to 4% · 0 from 0% to 2% · -1 from -2% to 0% · -2 below -2%.

indicators.measure: Japan unemployment rate (latest month against the previous month)
indicators.where_to_find: Statistics Bureau of Japan → Labour Force Survey (latest monthly release) → unemployment rate, seasonally adjusted, for the latest month and the previous month. The jobs-to-applicants ratio is context only.
indicators.scoring_guide: A jobs-to-applicants ratio above 1.0 = tight labour market. Score the change in the unemployment rate (latest published rate against the previous published rate, both as shown by the source, to one decimal): +2 fell by 0.2 point or more · +1 fell by 0.1 point · 0 unchanged · -1 rose by 0.1 point · -2 rose by 0.2 point or more. Employment change is context only.

indicators.measure: General government gross debt, % of GDP (IMF World Economic Outlook, series GGXWDG_NGDP)
indicators.where_to_find: IMF DataMapper (open the JSON file at the source address; the same series is on imf.org/external/datamapper/GGXWDG_NGDP). Read the values for JPN for the last completed calendar year and the year before it. Ignore the current year and later years, which are forecasts. State which World Economic Outlook edition the data comes from.
indicators.scoring_guide: The very high level is structural, so only the change is scored. Score the change over the last year (last completed calendar year against the year before): +1 falling or stable (no rise) · 0 rising by less than 1 point of GDP · -1 rising by 1 to 4 points · -2 rising by more than 4 points.

indicators.measure: General government net lending (+) / borrowing (-), % of GDP (IMF World Economic Outlook, series GGXCNL_NGDP; a negative number is a deficit)
indicators.where_to_find: IMF DataMapper (open the JSON file at the source address; the same series is on imf.org/external/datamapper/GGXCNL_NGDP). Read the values for JPN for the last completed calendar year and the year before it. Ignore the current year and later years, which are forecasts. State which World Economic Outlook edition the data comes from.
indicators.scoring_guide: Score the change in the budget balance as a % of GDP (latest full year against the year before): +1 surplus, or deficit narrowed by 0.5 point or more · 0 deficit moved by less than 0.5 point · -1 deficit widened by 0.5 to 1.5 points · -2 deficit widened by more than 1.5 points (a surplus that falls into deficit counts as widening).

indicators.where_to_find: Japan Ministry of Finance → JGB yields table (daily) → the '10-year' column → read the latest day and the same column a week earlier.
indicators.scoring_guide: Rising = BoJ normalization = JPY bullish; falling = BoJ capping yields (YCC) = JPY bearish. Score the change in the yield over the last 7 days (latest daily value against the value on the same weekday one week earlier, or the nearest earlier trading day): +2 up more than 0.25 point · +1 up 0.05 to 0.25 · 0 moved by less than 0.05 either way · -1 down 0.05 to 0.25 · -2 down more than 0.25 point.

indicators.where_to_find: FRED → JPNASSETS (Bank of Japan total assets, monthly) → read the latest value and the value from the same month a year earlier.
indicators.scoring_guide: Shrinking = normalization = hawkish; aggressive expansion = JPY bearish. Score the change in total assets (the ratio to GDP is not needed) over the last year, latest weekly or monthly figure against the same date a year earlier: +2 down more than 10% · +1 down 2% to 10% · 0 moved by less than 2% either way · -1 up 2% to 10% · -2 up more than 10%.

indicators.where_to_find: Procure.ch → Latest PMI release. Site may be in German — look for the numeric PMI value in the headline.
indicators.scoring_guide: Swiss PMI mirrors Eurozone trends. Score the headline PMI reading: +2 above 52 · +1 from 50.5 to 52 · 0 from 49.5 to 50.5 · -1 from 47 to 49.5 · -2 below 47.

indicators.where_to_find: S&P Global PMI → Filter 'Switzerland Services' → PMI headline figure.
indicators.scoring_guide: Switzerland is a service-dominated economy. Score the headline PMI reading: +2 above 54 · +1 from 51 to 54 · 0 from 50 to 51 · -1 from 47 to 50 · -2 below 47.

indicators.where_to_find: SECO → Consumer Sentiment → Quarterly index. Negative values are normal for Switzerland.
indicators.scoring_guide: +2 strongly rising · +1 improving · 0 stable · -1 falling · -2 sharply deteriorating.

indicators.where_to_find: Swiss Federal Statistics → Construction → Building permits latest monthly figure. Also find the same month a year earlier, so the change over the year can be worked out (calculate the % change yourself if the page does not show it).
indicators.scoring_guide: Swiss housing market is stable — changes matter. Score the change over the last year (latest month against the same month a year earlier), not the change from last month: +2 up more than 10% · +1 up 2% to 10% · 0 moved by less than 2% either way · -1 down 2% to 10% · -2 down more than 10%.

indicators.measure: Swiss M2 Money Supply (SNB monetary aggregates)
indicators.where_to_find: SNB data portal → Monetary aggregates (cube snbmonagg) → M2, latest monthly level and the level for the same month a year earlier. If the portal does not show the year-on-year % change, work it out yourself. The old FRED Swiss M2 series is out of date, so do not use it.
indicators.scoring_guide: Score the year-on-year growth of M2: +2 above 4% · +1 from 2% to 4% · 0 from 0% to 2% · -1 from -2% to 0% · -2 below -2%.

indicators.hub_name: Central Bank Rate & Current Policy Stance
indicators.where_to_find: SNB → 'SNB policy rate' in the interest rate table. Check latest quarterly assessment for direction.
indicators.scoring_guide: Score the latest SNB quarterly assessment: +2 raised the policy rate · +1 held and signalled that a rise is possible · 0 held and said policy remains appropriate · -1 held and said it is ready to ease or to act in the currency market · -2 cut the rate, or clearly signalled a move to negative rates. Judge the latest meeting only; earlier moves do not count.

indicators.where_to_find: Swiss Federal Statistics → CPI → Annual % change rate in the latest release.
indicators.scoring_guide: SNB targets 0-2%. Score the headline annual rate: +2 above 2% · +1 from 1.5% to 2% · 0 from 0.5% to 1.5% · -1 from 0% to 0.5% · -2 below 0%.

indicators.where_to_find: Same Swiss Statistics CPI page → Core CPI (ex energy and seasonal items) annual % change.
indicators.scoring_guide: Swiss core inflation rarely spikes; a sustained rise is a rare hawkish SNB signal. Score the annual rate with the same bands as headline CPI: +2 above 2% · +1 from 1.5% to 2% · 0 from 0.5% to 1.5% · -1 from 0% to 0.5% · -2 below 0%.

indicators.where_to_find: Swiss Federal Statistics → Producer & Import Price Index → Annual % change.
indicators.scoring_guide: Swiss PPI includes import prices, which matters given the franc's effect on import costs. Score the annual rate: +2 above 4% · +1 from 2% to 4% · 0 from 0% to 2% · -1 from -2% to 0% · -2 below -2%.

indicators.measure: Swiss domestic producer prices (producer price index excluding imports), annual % change
indicators.where_to_find: Swiss Federal Statistics → Producer and import price index → 'Domestic products' (producer prices excluding imports) annual % change. Give the month it covers.
indicators.scoring_guide: Domestic price pressure excluding imports. Score the annual rate with the same bands as headline PPI: +2 above 4% · +1 from 2% to 4% · 0 from 0% to 2% · -1 from -2% to 0% · -2 below -2%.

indicators.measure: Swiss unemployment rate (latest quarter against the previous quarter)
indicators.where_to_find: Swiss Federal Statistics → Employment → unemployment rate (ILO definition, seasonally adjusted) for the latest quarter and the previous quarter.
indicators.scoring_guide: Switzerland has one of the lowest unemployment rates globally, so only the change is scored. Score the change in the unemployment rate (latest published rate against the previous published rate, both as shown by the source, to one decimal): +2 fell by 0.2 point or more · +1 fell by 0.1 point · 0 unchanged · -1 rose by 0.1 point · -2 rose by 0.2 point or more. Employment change is context only.

indicators.measure: General government gross debt, % of GDP (IMF World Economic Outlook, series GGXWDG_NGDP)
indicators.where_to_find: IMF DataMapper (open the JSON file at the source address; the same series is on imf.org/external/datamapper/GGXWDG_NGDP). Read the values for CHE for the last completed calendar year and the year before it. Ignore the current year and later years, which are forecasts. State which World Economic Outlook edition the data comes from.
indicators.scoring_guide: Debt is very low, so only the change is scored. Score the change over the last year (last completed calendar year against the year before): +1 falling or stable (no rise) · 0 rising by less than 1 point of GDP · -1 rising by 1 to 4 points · -2 rising by more than 4 points.

indicators.measure: General government net lending (+) / borrowing (-), % of GDP (IMF World Economic Outlook, series GGXCNL_NGDP; a negative number is a deficit)
indicators.where_to_find: IMF DataMapper (open the JSON file at the source address; the same series is on imf.org/external/datamapper/GGXCNL_NGDP). Read the values for CHE for the last completed calendar year and the year before it. Ignore the current year and later years, which are forecasts. State which World Economic Outlook edition the data comes from.
indicators.scoring_guide: Switzerland often runs surpluses. Score the change in the budget balance as a % of GDP (latest full year against the year before): +1 surplus, or deficit narrowed by 0.5 point or more · 0 deficit moved by less than 0.5 point · -1 deficit widened by 0.5 to 1.5 points · -2 deficit widened by more than 1.5 points (a surplus that falls into deficit counts as widening).

indicators.where_to_find: SNB → Current interest rates and exchange rates → Interest rates → yield on Swiss Confederation bonds, spot rate for 10-year maturities (daily). For the value a week earlier use the SNB data portal (data.snb.ch) series for Confederation bond yields, 10 years, daily.
indicators.scoring_guide: Swiss yields can be near zero or negative; only the change is scored. Score the change in the yield over the last 7 days (latest daily value against the value on the same weekday one week earlier, or the nearest earlier trading day): +2 up more than 0.25 point · +1 up 0.05 to 0.25 · 0 moved by less than 0.05 either way · -1 down 0.05 to 0.25 · -2 down more than 0.25 point.

indicators.where_to_find: SNB Balance Sheet → Total assets (monthly) → read the latest figure and the one from the same month a year earlier.
indicators.scoring_guide: Growth often reflects FX intervention; the SNB has one of the largest balance sheets relative to GDP. Score the change in total assets (the ratio to GDP is not needed) over the last year, latest weekly or monthly figure against the same date a year earlier: +2 down more than 10% · +1 down 2% to 10% · 0 moved by less than 2% either way · -1 up 2% to 10% · -2 up more than 10%.

indicators.where_to_find: S&P Global PMI → Filter 'Canada Manufacturing' → PMI headline figure in latest release.
indicators.scoring_guide: Heavily linked to US demand and commodity prices. Score the headline PMI reading: +2 above 52 · +1 from 50.5 to 52 · 0 from 49.5 to 50.5 · -1 from 47 to 49.5 · -2 below 47.

indicators.where_to_find: Same site → Filter 'Canada Services' → PMI headline figure.
indicators.scoring_guide: Score the headline PMI reading: +2 above 54 · +1 from 51 to 54 · 0 from 50 to 51 · -1 from 47 to 50 · -2 below 47.

indicators.where_to_find: Conference Board of Canada → Consumer Confidence Index. Monthly headline figure.
indicators.scoring_guide: +2 strongly rising · +1 improving · 0 stable · -1 falling · -2 sharply deteriorating.

indicators.where_to_find: Statistics Canada → Building permits → Monthly value in billions of dollars. Also find the same month a year earlier, so the change over the year can be worked out (calculate the % change yourself if the page does not show it).
indicators.scoring_guide: Canada housing = key economic driver. Score the change over the last year (latest month against the same month a year earlier), not the change from last month: +2 up more than 10% · +1 up 2% to 10% · 0 moved by less than 2% either way · -1 down 2% to 10% · -2 down more than 10%.

indicators.where_to_find: FRED → Canada M2 series → Annual growth rate. Note if expanding or contracting.
indicators.scoring_guide: Score the year-on-year growth of M2: +2 above 5% · +1 from 2% to 5% · 0 from 0% to 2% · -1 from -2% to 0% · -2 below -2%.

indicators.hub_name: Central Bank Rate & Current Policy Stance
indicators.where_to_find: Bank of Canada → Target overnight rate shown in LARGE TEXT at top. Check latest statement for direction.
indicators.scoring_guide: Score the latest BoC decision and statement: +2 raised the rate, or held while clearly signalling the next move is a rise · +1 held with the statement leaning hawkish (rates may need to stay high) · 0 held with a balanced message · -1 held with the statement leaning dovish (cuts likely) · -2 cut the rate. Judge the latest meeting only; earlier moves do not count.

indicators.where_to_find: Statistics Canada → Consumer Price Index → '12-month change, All-items' % in the latest release.
indicators.scoring_guide: BoC targets 2%. Score the headline annual rate: +2 above 3.5% · +1 from 2.5% to 3.5% · 0 from 1.5% to 2.5% · -1 from 1% to 1.5% · -2 below 1%.

indicators.where_to_find: BoC Inflation page → CPI-Trim and CPI-Median both shown. Record both and average them.
indicators.scoring_guide: BoC uses both trim and median as core measures. Average the two readings first, then score the average. Score the annual rate with the same bands as headline CPI: +2 above 3.5% · +1 from 2.5% to 3.5% · 0 from 1.5% to 2.5% · -1 from 1% to 1.5% · -2 below 1%.

indicators.where_to_find: Statistics Canada → Industrial Product Price Index (IPPI) → Annual % change.
indicators.scoring_guide: IPPI leads CPI by 1-3 months. Rising = inflationary pipeline = BoC stays hawkish. Score the annual rate: +2 above 4% · +1 from 2% to 4% · 0 from 0% to 2% · -1 from -2% to 0% · -2 below -2%.

indicators.measure: Canada IPPI excluding energy and petroleum products, annual % change
indicators.where_to_find: Statistics Canada → Industrial product price index (latest monthly release) → IPPI excluding energy and petroleum products → 12-month % change. Give the month it covers.
indicators.scoring_guide: Core IPPI strips out oil volatility. Score the annual rate with the same bands as headline PPI: +2 above 4% · +1 from 2% to 4% · 0 from 0% to 2% · -1 from -2% to 0% · -2 below -2%.

indicators.where_to_find: Statistics Canada → Labour Force Survey → Employment change in thousands AND unemployment rate %.
indicators.scoring_guide: +2 strong jobs beat + falling unemployment · +1 beat · 0 in line · -1 miss · -2 large miss.

indicators.measure: General government gross debt, % of GDP (IMF World Economic Outlook, series GGXWDG_NGDP)

Read the values for CAN for the last completed calendar year and the year before it. Ignore the current year and later years, which are forecasts. indicators.where_to_find: Bank of Canada → Canadian bonds → Selected benchmark bond yields → the 10-year row → read the latest day and the value from a week earlier (the 10-year lookup page on the same site goes further back).
indicators.scoring_guide: Compare the move with the US 10-year as context only. Score the change in the yield over the last 7 days (latest daily value against the value on the same weekday one week earlier, or the nearest earlier trading day): +2 up more than 0.25 point · +1 up 0.05 to 0.25 · 0 moved by less than 0.05 either way · -1 down 0.05 to 0.25 · -2 down more than 0.25 point.

indicators.where_to_find: BoC weekly balance sheet → Total assets → read the latest figure and the one from the same week a year earlier.
indicators.scoring_guide: Shrinking = QT. Score the change in total assets (the ratio to GDP is not needed) over the last year, latest weekly or monthly figure against the same date a year earlier: +2 down more than 10% · +1 down 2% to 10% · 0 moved by less than 2% either way · -1 up 2% to 10% · -2 up more than 10%.

indicators.where_to_find: S&P Global PMI → Filter 'Australia Manufacturing' (Judo Bank PMI) → PMI headline figure.
indicators.scoring_guide: AUD PMI tracks China demand. Score the headline PMI reading: +2 above 52 · +1 from 50.5 to 52 · 0 from 49.5 to 50.5 · -1 from 47 to 49.5 · -2 below 47.

indicators.where_to_find: Same site → Filter 'Australia Services' (Judo Bank) → PMI headline figure.
indicators.scoring_guide: Score the headline PMI reading: +2 above 54 · +1 from 51 to 54 · 0 from 50 to 51 · -1 from 47 to 50 · -2 below 47.

indicators.where_to_find: Westpac-Melbourne Institute Consumer Sentiment → Monthly index. Below 100 = pessimistic majority.
indicators.scoring_guide: +2 above 105 & rising · +1 above 100 · 0 near 100 · -1 below 95 · -2 below 90 & falling.

indicators.where_to_find: ABS Building Approvals → Monthly number of dwellings approved. Also find the same month a year earlier, so the change over the year can be worked out (calculate the % change yourself if the page does not show it).
indicators.scoring_guide: Score the change over the last year (latest month against the same month a year earlier), not the change from last month: +2 up more than 10% · +1 up 2% to 10% · 0 moved by less than 2% either way · -1 down 2% to 10% · -2 down more than 10%.

indicators.where_to_find: FRED → Australia M2 series → Annual growth rate.
indicators.scoring_guide: Score the year-on-year growth of M2: +2 above 6% · +1 from 2% to 6% · 0 from 0% to 2% · -1 from -2% to 0% · -2 below -2%.

indicators.hub_name: Central Bank Rate & Current Policy Stance
indicators.where_to_find: RBA → Cash rate target shown in LARGE COLOURED BOX at top. Check latest statement for direction.
indicators.scoring_guide: Score the latest RBA decision and statement: +2 raised the rate, or held while clearly signalling the next move is a rise · +1 held with the statement leaning hawkish (rates may need to stay high) · 0 held with a balanced message · -1 held with the statement leaning dovish (cuts likely) · -2 cut the rate. Judge the latest meeting only; earlier moves do not count.

indicators.scoring_guide: RBA targets 2-3%. Score the headline annual rate: +2 above 4% · +1 from 3% to 4% · 0 from 2% to 3% · -1 from 1.5% to 2% · -2 below 1.5%.

indicators.where_to_find: Same ABS CPI release → 'Trimmed mean' annual % change — this is RBA's preferred core measure.
indicators.scoring_guide: RBA watches the trimmed mean most closely. Score the annual rate with the same bands as headline CPI: +2 above 4% · +1 from 3% to 4% · 0 from 2% to 3% · -1 from 1.5% to 2% · -2 below 1.5%.

indicators.where_to_find: ABS PPI → Producer Price Index quarterly release → Annual % change for final demand.
indicators.scoring_guide: Rising PPI = inflationary pipeline building. Quarterly release: use the latest quarter. Score the annual rate: +2 above 4% · +1 from 2% to 4% · 0 from 0% to 2% · -1 from -2% to 0% · -2 below -2%.

indicators.measure: Australia PPI, output of the manufacturing industries, annual % change
indicators.where_to_find: ABS Producer Price Indexes (latest quarterly release) → Output of the manufacturing industries → annual % change. Give the quarter it covers.
indicators.scoring_guide: Core pipeline pressure outside the commodity swings. Quarterly release: use the latest quarter. Score the annual rate with the same bands as headline PPI: +2 above 4% · +1 from 2% to 4% · 0 from 0% to 2% · -1 from -2% to 0% · -2 below -2%.

carry_trade.real_rate_differential: (Target policy rate - Target CPI YoY) - (Funding policy rate - Funding CPI YoY)

fields: score (0-10 conviction; 10 max hawkish, 0 max dovish, 5 neutral)

facts: Policy Rate % and direction (Hiking / Hold-Hawkish / Hold-Neutral / Hold-Dovish / Cutting)

cot.source: CFTC Traders in Financial Futures (TFF), Leveraged Funds. Released Fridays 3:30 PM ET.

known_gaps: Volatility (10% weight) is not collected by the weekly pipeline; it is still entered by hand.
ISM Manufacturing and Services PMI for the USD are typed in by hand each month (ism_fetcher.py); no free API.

The Exogenous layer in the pipeline is four structural facts (GDP, current account, policy rate, stock index). Older manual materials list oil, copper, China PMI, VIX, DXY and geopolitics. Decide which is the standard.

Government debt and fiscal balance for GBP, JPY, CHF, CAD, AUD and NZD come from the IMF World Economic Outlook, which is updated in April and October; the latest full year is an estimate and can be revised.
